question: Dechomai Asset Trust (EIN 260724604) FY2021: Schedule D Part I line 4 is $267.7m against Part X net assets of $1,148.1m (object 202243199349331259; ratio 23.3% vs 60.3% in FY2020 and 100.0% in FY2022, contributions and grants 100% DAF in all three years). Read Dechomai's audited statements for 2021 (or 2022 with comparatives) and the FY2022 return's prior-year figures to settle whether line 4 or Part X is right; also test FY2020, whose 60.3% ratio is itself out of line
conclusion_affected: FY2021 corrected market total ($234.01bn vs $234.79bn sensitivity), FY2020->21 growth (38.7% vs 39.1%), FY2021->22 growth (-2.5% vs -2.8%)
rationale: The only listed break besides NPT FY2023. The filed value is more than 70% below both the forward ($935.2m) and backward ($1,148.2m) roll-forwards; the two roll-forwards differ by 19%, partly because the FY2020 anchor may also be understated

question: Re-run the NPT-pattern screen for FY2024 once FY2025 Form 990s are in the IRS index (index_2026 and index_2027): only 783 of 1,512 FY2024 sponsor-years could be tested against both neighbours ($216.6bn of $327.9bn DAFRC value); the one-sided supplement found no break above $250m
conclusion_affected: Corrected FY2024 market total ($323.27bn) and FY2023->24 growth
rationale: Fidelity, Schwab-sized and most CF FY2025 returns are filed in May-November 2026, so FY2024 coverage grows each month; the screen is scripted and reruns in about a minute from the parse cache

question: Sub-threshold NPT-pattern breaks that fail the roll-forward: Servant Foundation FY2022 (filed $1,153.9m, roll midpoint about $1,355.9m), Thrivent Charitable FY2021 (-$118.2m), BNY Mellon Charitable Gift Fund FY2022 (-$67.8m), FJC FY2021 (-$61.5m). Check each against audited statements and decide whether a repo rule for filed-but-inconsistent line 4 values (beyond NPT's SENS row) is warranted
conclusion_affected: Corrected FY2021-22 market totals (combined about -$450m of filed understatement in these four)
rationale: 29 NPT-pattern sponsor-years fail the roll-forward; outside NPT and Dechomai they sum to about +$29m net but include four understatements of $60m-$200m each at national or faith sponsors

question: Realised admin-fee rates for all 641 tail CFs from Form 990 alone: apply the fee-line method (Part VIII revenue lines named administrative/management fees, Schedule D Part XI line 2d administrative-fee items, Schedule D Part V line 1f) to every tail CF FY2022-24, classify capture (internal vs agency/unknown) from the filer's wording, and replace the schedule-based pool with a realised-rate pool
conclusion_affected: Choice between the whole-tail ($138m) and CFs-only ($90m) pool; whether the realised all-fund rate (median about 104 bps where internal fees are disclosed) or the published DAF rate (150 bps) should anchor it
rationale: In the 31-CF sample, 22 show some fee income on the 990 and 8 disclose internal fees charged to funds; the method needs no website access, so robots-blocked sponsors (5 of 31 CFs) are covered

question: Realised fees at non-CF tail sponsors (religious, single-issue, university/hospital, nationals; $3.08bn of tail DAF assets): run the same 990 fee-line read on the 29 non-CF sponsors in the census sample to test the whole-tail pool's assumption that non-CFs charge CF-type prices
conclusion_affected: Whole-tail pool ($138m) vs CFs-only ($90m); the $108m mixed case in wave 35A
rationale: This study covered CFs only, as the queue item specified; the non-CF half of the pool assumption is still unobserved

question: DAF-specific realised fees: for the tail CFs whose audits or 990s disclose internal fees (Hutchinson, Decatur County, Clinton County OH, Four Way, Monroe, Greene County PA, Licking County), look for fund-type detail (supplementary schedules by fund type, board-approved fee policies in minutes, or the fund-type split of Schedule D Part V) to separate DAF fee income from endowed and agency funds
conclusion_affected: Whether tail DAF fees run above the all-fund realised rate (Hutchinson: 83 bps realised on all funds vs 125 bps published DAF rate)
rationale: Every realised rate here is all-fund; fee income divided by average DAF balance is only an upper bound (e.g. Hutchinson 312 bps), so the DAF rate itself is still unobserved
